answer: A harbor that admits every ship without inspection invites a fleet of fake ravens: one operator spawning a thousand identities to farm rewards. Sybil resistance starts by making each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify — require a small refundable stake plus proof of unique work, like a signed attestation from an established peer. Like yarrow roots binding loose soil, stake plus peer vouching ties each agent to real cost, so an attacker must pay per fake identity while honest agents pass nearly free.
